issues.claim: The port's statement of how dossier events meet locks disagrees with the base precedence that this round rewrote. Base §7.7 (l.11371-11382, VEL0-01) says a dossier event 'is never refused by a lock or a pin'. A lock or pin on what the event changes (a dossier-owned value; a dossier-backed element's existence, state, name, kind or membership) 'supersedes it for what it changes — the lock or pin reported orphaned'. Its examples: a dossier rename lands on a locked name path, and a `ruined`/`removed` state closes a locked building's use. Only 'a lock on anything else the event touches' is applied around. A population fall reaches locked and pinned dwellings by `relet`. V08 §4.3 (l.2560) instead says 'A dossier event mutates only its disruption set …, around every lock, pin, positive placement and declared entity'. V08 §3.3's absorb bullet (l.1496) says the events 'are never refused by map locks or pins, around which they apply'. Neither states the supersession or the population reach. An adapter built from V08 would keep a locked name against a dossier rename, which the base's T20 fixtures refuse.
issues.required_change: V08 §4.3's first sentence reads: 'A dossier event mutates only its disruption set (§7.7 item 5; T20-8) and is never refused by a lock or a pin (§7.7's precedence). A lock or pin on what it changes — a dossier-owned value, or a dossier-backed element's existence, state, name, kind or membership — is superseded for what it changes and reported orphaned, the dossier fact its `why`. Every other lock, pin, positive placement and declared entity is applied around, and a population fall reaches locked and pinned dwellings by `relet` (§7.7's precedence; V06 §3.5.1 (4)). An edit it can no longer honour is reported and orphaned, never dropped (J-A20.73).' V08 §3.3's absorb bullet reads '— never refused by map locks or pins (§7.7's precedence: a lock on what a dossier event changes is superseded and reported orphaned, every other applied around) —'.
